items.name: Google Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Google's new top-tier frontier model anchoring the Gemini 4 generation, larger than its previous Pro line and posting leading marks on DeepSWE, Vals Index, AutomationBench and LVBench. Biggest technical jump is 1M-token output (up from 64k); initial access is limited to vetted cyber defenders via the Fairwind program and the US government before wider release.

items.name: OpenAI Decisions API
items.summary: Announced at DevDay on September 29: a special version of GPT-6 Luna that, instead of generating text, scores a developer's fixed list of answers and returns one choice with a confidence score in ~150 ms (vs ~1.6 s for a standard call). In limited preview; OpenAI's direct answer to TypeSafe AI's Jev for classification, routing and agent-control tasks.

items.name: Cloudflare Clef
items.summary: Released October 1: two open-weight decision models (27B Clef and 9B Clef-flash) that return probabilities for typed yes/no/choice/score questions instead of generating text — no token-by-token generation, so Clef-flash answers in ~39 ms. Apache 2.0 weights on Hugging Face, Jev-API compatible, with vision input and a new RL fine-tuning platform.

items.name: AWS Strands Decider 2B
items.summary: Released October 1 from AWS Strands Labs: a fully open-source ~2B-parameter decision model built on Qwen3.5-2B, replacing the text head with a ~1M-parameter 'pointer head' that scores predefined options with calibrated confidence in under 100 ms locally. Weights, training data and scripts published under Apache 2.0 — a free, self-hostable alternative to TypeSafe's API-only Jev.

items.name: Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5.5
items.summary: Launched September 28: the second model in the Claude 5.5 family runs over 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and costs up to 30% less per task at the same $2/$10 per-million-token pricing. Strongest at everyday coding, docs, slides and design work, and the first Sonnet to ship with cyber safeguards comparable to Anthropic's flagship models.
